newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Wall Street gives Singapore stocks an early boost.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street gives Singapore stocks an early boost.

text.p: The Singapore stock market got an early lift Wednesday morning from Wall Street's firmer close overnight but caution capped upside potential, dealers said.
At 0230 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was up 3.69 points at 1,993.89 while the property index was up 6.88 points or 1.06 percent at 653.84.

Property stocks bounced as fears of more property curbs by the government receded. Property blue chip City Developments rose S$0.30 to S$11.80 on 976,000 million shares. The stock was also lifted by the news it brought a prime hotel site late Tuesday. The Boulevard hotel has redevelopment potential.
Dealers said there were some nibbling of selected blue chips in the banking and property sectors as well as under-valued stocks.
But they said the upside was capped by overall market caution despite Wall Street's 179-point rise overnight.
Singapore Press Foreign, which had fallen recently, led gainers, rising S$0.40 to S$26.90. Foreign tranches of banks like UOB, DBS and OUB were also higher.
Malaysia's Renong Bhd was the most active with over 2.7 million shares. Total market volume was a moderate 37 million units with 178 up against 41 down. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
